bottleneck: Gene therapy regulation differs across the FDA, EMA, and other agencies in requirements for vector characterization, long-term follow-up, and germline risk assessment. Developers must run parallel, sometimes contradictory, programs for each market, multiplying cost and delay beyond what small patient populations can support. Evolving rules for novel modalities like in vivo editing add uncertainty on top of fragmentation, and guidance often arrives after pivotal trials are designed.
current_state: Regulators are issuing new guidance (e.g., FDA's 2026 chromosomal-integrity recommendations), but harmonization efforts move slowly while the technology races ahead. Developers plan for the strictest regulator by default.

title: Fragmented global regulation of gene therapies
why_it_blocks: Cures delayed by paperwork are cures denied. Regulatory fragmentation taxes every program with duplicated effort, pricing the smallest patient populations out of development entirely and slowing access everywhere else.
